name: Okonkwo-Paz Night — The Lakefire Collapse of 2211
creator: Lakefire Cultural Consortium (Tier 2-3 community org)
description: The Lakefire Multicultural Music & Food Festival's 2211 edition, headlined by sonic architect Celestine Okonkwo-Paz, drew an estimated 80,000 attendees to the reclaimed lakefront when a structural failure in the repurposed pier network sent three floating stages into Lake Michigan over the course of ninety minutes. Emergency response was delayed by a corporate jurisdiction dispute between Axiom and the Municipal Safety Directorate. Forty-four people died; over three hundred were injured.
medium: live event, neural-captured by thousands of attendees
cultural_impact: The disaster exposed the lethal consequences of overlapping corporate sovereignty in public emergency response and became the central case study in the Meridian Infrastructure Liability Reform hearings of 2213.
controversy: Celestine Okonkwo-Paz, who survived and pulled survivors from the water, was initially charged with unlicensed neural broadcast after attendee BCI footage was aggregated without consent; charges were later dropped under public pressure.
story_hooks: An engineer who signed off on the pier inspection is living quietly in Tier 1 under a different name.
The aggregated BCI footage from 80,000 attendees has never been fully processed — somewhere in the data is a clear record of who knew the structure was failing.
Celestine Okonkwo-Paz has not performed publicly since 2211 but has been seen entering a Shelf recording space late at night.
